title: MmConfig

agents.description: What an AI agent may do through `mm mcp serve`, per environment.

hardening.description:
`strict` hardens every service of a deployment: read-only root
filesystem, no capabilities, no new privileges, the engine's default
seccomp profile, a tmpfs at `/tmp`. Not applied by `mm dev`.

registries.description: Image registries and the credentials deploys pull with, by host.

release-inputs.description:
Values `mm deploy plan --release-input NAME=VALUE` supplies per
deployment, read as `RELEASE.<NAME>`.

targets.description: Public connection facts for remote targets; clients pin them.

users.description: Who may reach each remote environment, reconciled on deploy.

$comment: Generated from MmConfig; run ./scripts/generate-artifacts.sh. Do not edit.

AccessLevel.description: Access levels a repo grants per environment. Each includes the previous.

oneOf.description: `view` plus restart and job run, cancel, and retry.
`operate` plus deploy, rollback, and team sync.

`deploy` plus exec, forward, setting secrets and variables,
emergency blocks, and audit.

AgentAccess.description: What an agent may do in one environment.

exec.description: Services the agent may run commands in: `true`, or a list of names.

secrets.description:
The agent may set secrets and variables on the environment's hosts
for the next deployment, when its user may. With level `deploy` on an
environment that runs on this machine, it may also create the local
secret store, generate missing secrets, and install a managed secret
provider. It never reads a value.

AgentAccessConfig.description: `production: view` or `local: { level: deploy, exec: true }`.

AllowRule.description:
One kind of request a route lets through: one of `methods` (any when
empty) whose path matches `path` (any when absent).

methods.description: HTTP methods in capitals, such as `[GET, HEAD]`.

path.description:
A regular expression the request path matches, such as
`^/hooks/[^/]+$`.

metric.description:
What is measured and when a container is added or removed. Every
key has a default: CPU, up above 75% for 30s, down below 40% for 5m.

scale.description: How few and how many containers the service runs.

Balance.description:
Which of a service's healthy containers an ingress node sends a route's
requests to.

oneOf.description: The ones on the proxy's own node, and every node's when it has none.

BuildTarget.description:
A build target under `modules.<m>.build.targets`, which an environment's
`build-variant` selects: the tag suffix alone, or a mapping.

args.description: Build arguments merged over the module's `build.args`.

suffix.description: The image tag suffix; defaults to the target's name.

target.description: The Dockerfile stage; defaults to the target's name.

CloudflaredConfig.description: The Cloudflare Tunnel of an environment with `type: cloudflared`.

image.description:
The connector's image. The default is a cloudflared release mm
pins by digest.

token.description:
The secret that holds the tunnel's token, as
`cloudflared tunnel token <name>` prints it.

Delivery.description: How a target's hosts get a commit's files.

oneOf.description: Each host fetches the commit from the origin in its host policy.

mm sends the commit's tracked files; the hosts never contact the
git server.

convergence-timeout.description:
How long a stack may take on a host to become healthy before the
deployment counts as failed, such as `90s` or `15m`. The default is
`10m`. The plan shows it.

mm-version.description:
The releases of mm that may plan deployments here, and that the
hosts' mmd must be: `0.9` is any 0.9 release, `=0.9.3` exactly that
one. A plan from another mm, or for a host that runs another mmd,
is refused, and `mm doctor` reports both. Not set: any mm that
speaks the hosts' protocol.

progress-timeout.description:
How long `mm deploy apply` waits without any sign of progress from
a host before it stops with a timeout that names the host, the step
and the operation, such as `5m`. The default is `2m`; at least `30s`.

Development.description: Whether a module, service or job runs in the development environment.

source.description: Relative to the module path, like the primary source.

additional.description: Additional source directories mounted into the same services with the same mode.

source.description: Relative to the module path, never the workstation root.

target.description: Absolute POSIX path in the selected container services.

sensitive-patterns.description: Additional case-insensitive glob-like names (`*` matches any substring).

DownRuleConfig.description:
`autoscale.metric.down`: remove a container when the average is below
`less` for `for`.

EnvironmentAccess.description: One user's effective access in one environment.

deploy.description: How deployments to this environment behave.

deploy-from.description:
Branches a commit must be reachable from to be deployed here: names, or
patterns where `*` matches within one `/` segment (`*.x`); `*` alone is
any branch. A commit that changes this list must pass the current one.

tls.description:
A certificate the environment provides for its domains, in place
of one the ingress requests with ACME.

balance.description:
`local-first` (the default) sends each request to the service's
containers on the ingress node that took it, and to every node's
only when that node runs none; `spread` sends it to the service's
containers on every node.

headers.description:
Response headers every route of the environment sets on a cluster
target, such as `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.

type.description:
`public` (the default) takes requests on ports 80 and 443 of the
ingress nodes; `cloudflared` through a Cloudflare Tunnel, with no
port open. Local development ignores it.

EnvironmentTlsConfig.description:
A certificate the operator provides for an environment's domains, such
as a Cloudflare origin certificate, where ACME challenges cannot reach
the ingress. Both secrets hold a PEM file encoded as base64 on one line
(`base64 -w0 cert.pem | mm secret set NAME --stdin`).

oneOf.description:
Every service of a deployment gets a read-only root filesystem,
drops all Linux capabilities, cannot gain privileges, keeps the
engine's default seccomp profile, and gets a tmpfs at `/tmp`.

HardeningExceptions.description: Each key is a default the service leaves out; its value says why.

cap-drop.description:
Keep the engine's default capabilities. A service that needs a few
keeps them with `cap_add` in its Compose file and needs no
exception.

no-new-privileges.description: Let processes gain privileges through setuid binaries.

read-only.description:
Keep the root filesystem writable. Volumes and bind mounts are
writable either way: prefer a volume for the paths the service
writes.

seccomp.description:
Let the Compose file choose another seccomp profile than the
engine's default.

after.description:
How long a container stays unhealthy before it is restarted, such as
`3m` (the default).

max-restarts.description:
How many restarts of one container within `window` before its node
stops restarting it; default 5.

on-failure.description:
`restart` (the default on a cluster target) restarts a container
that stays unhealthy; `none` leaves it as it is.

allow.description:
On a cluster target: the only requests that reach the service; the
proxy answers 404 to every other one.

balance.description:
On a cluster target: `spread` sends this route's requests to the
service's containers on every node. The default is the
environment's `ingress.balance`, else `spread` for a service with
`autoscale` and `local-first` for every other one.

headers.description:
On a cluster target: response headers, on top of the environment's
`ingress.headers`. An empty value removes the header.

priority.description:
On a cluster target: where this route stands among the routes of
its host, from 1 to 1000000. By default the longer path goes first.

IngressType.description: Where an environment's requests come in on a cluster target.

oneOf.description: Ports 80 and 443 of every ingress node.
A Cloudflare Tunnel, with no port open on any node.

Ipv4Cidr.description: An IPv4 network in CIDR notation, such as 10.90.0.0/24.

development.description:
`on` (the default), `optional` or `off` in the development
environment. A job of a service that is off is off too.

environments.description:
The environments the job belongs to; every environment when left
out. `environment:` with one name is read the same way.

placement.description:
On a cluster target, the node the job runs on: a node name, or a
group whose first node that runs the service is taken. It must run
the job's service. Without it, the first node that does.

run.description:
When a deployment runs the job by itself: `before-deploy` (before
its service is started or replaced, after what the service depends
on is healthy), `after-deploy` (once the deployment converged), or
`once` (the first time the environment is deployed with it). Left
out, the job runs only when asked (`mm job run`) or scheduled.

user.description:
Who the command runs as in the container (`uid`, `uid:gid`, or a
name the image knows), in place of the service's own user.

JobEnvironments.description: One environment name, or a list of them.

JobWhen.description: When a deployment runs a job.

interface.description:
Use this existing private interface (`eth1`) instead of creating a
WireGuard mesh. Every node then declares its `private-address`.

mtu.description:
The mesh interface's MTU: the underlay's MTU minus 80 bytes of
WireGuard overhead. Default `1420`, which fits a 1500-byte underlay.

port.description:
The UDP port WireGuard listens on, on every node. It must be reachable
between the nodes. Default `51820`.

subnet.description: The WireGuard mesh's address range. Default `10.90.0.0/24`.

credential-only-secrets.description:
Keys of `secrets` that only authenticate fetching inputs, such as a
package registry token. They are still mounted, but they do not change
the image, so they never block reuse or promotion of a build.

development.description:
`on` (the default), `optional` (off in the development environment
until a developer turns it on with `mm dev enable`), or `off`. Its
services take it unless they set their own.

internal.description:
Containers on the network reach its members and nothing else: no
outbound access.

PlacementSpec.description: One placement word, or a list of them.

installation.description: Local development only. Default: the provider's name.

nodes.description:
Cluster targets only: the store's Raft members. Default: every
node of the target, when it has 3 or 5.

oneOf.description:
One store per environment: on a cluster target, the store mm runs
on the target's nodes.

ReferenceBinding.description: A release fact under another key: `value-ref: MM.RELEASE`.

RegistryConfig.description: A registry, keyed by its host (`ghcr.io`, `registry.example.com:5000`).

password.description: The secret holding the password or access token; set it per environment.

username.description: The account the token belongs to. GHCR accepts any name with a token.

ReleaseInputConfig.description:
One value under `release-inputs:` that `mm deploy plan` takes with
`--release-input NAME=VALUE`.

pattern.description:
A regular expression the whole value has to match, such as
`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`. Without one, any value of printable text is
accepted.

key.description: `ssh-ed25519 AAAA… comment`; keep the private half offline.

RepoClusterConfig.description: How the nodes of a cluster target work together. Every key has a default.

groups.description: Names for sets of nodes, for a service's `placement`.

ingress.description:
The nodes that run the ingress proxy and take the traffic of every
`ingress:` route, written like a `placement`: a node, a group,
`all`, or a list. Unset means the first node.

mesh.description:
The private network between the nodes: a WireGuard mesh mm creates
(`subnet`, `port`, `mtu`) or an existing `interface`.

networks.description:
Address space for networks that span the nodes: a private range, a
/20 or larger, that no node uses for anything else. Each network
takes a /20 of it (16 nodes, room for 253 containers on each), so
the default holds 256 networks.

storage.description: The node that serves shared volumes. Unset means the first node.

public-key.description: Its public half, as added to the git host.

secret.description:
The age secret holding the private key (`mm target setup deploy-key`
creates it).

RepoTargetConfig.description:
A repo target takes one of two forms. The flat form names one host. The
cluster form lists `nodes` instead; `mm target setup` prepares them and
`mm target setup record` writes each node's keys and address back.

cluster.description: Cluster form: the nodes' private network, storage node, and groups.

delivery.description:
How the target's hosts get a commit's files. `push`: mm sends them
over its own connection and the hosts never contact the git server.
Default `fetch`: each host fetches from the origin.

host.description: Flat form: the host mm connects to.

host-key.description: The host's SSH public key, `<type> <base64>`; its fingerprint is derived.

nodes.description:
Cluster form: every node. Replaces `host`, `host-key`, and
`daemon-fingerprint`.

providers.description:
Where this target's hosts read an external secret provider, by the
provider's name under `providers:`. The hosts resolve the secrets
themselves; see `mmd secrets connect`.

setup.description: Cluster form: what setup installs on every node.

RepoTargetNode.description:
One host of a cluster target. `mm target setup record` fills `host-key`,
`daemon-fingerprint`, and `private-address`.

endpoint.description:
The address the other nodes send WireGuard packets to, when that is
not `host`: for example an address on a network the nodes share.

host.description: The public address or DNS name mm connects to.

name.description: The node's name and hostname: a lowercase hostname label.

private-address.description:
The node's address on the private network. Unset, mm assigns the
lowest free address of the mesh subnet.

RepoTargetSetup.description: What setup installs on every node of a cluster target.

break-glass.description: Recovery keys that are admin on every node.

deploy-key.description: The environment's read-only deploy key, shared by every node.

origin.description:
Git URL every node fetches the project from. Left out with
`delivery: push`, where the nodes fetch nothing.

origin-host-key.description: The git server's SSH host key, `<type> <base64>`; required for SSH origins.

user.description: The account setup connects as; the operator's mm key is authorized for it.

type.description:
`cpu` (the default) or `memory`: a share of the container's limit,
or of one core (CPU) or of the node's memory without one.

max.description: The most containers, over all the service's nodes.

min.description: The fewest containers; defaults to the service's `replicas`.

generate.description: Present for generated secrets created by `mm secret generate`. Omit for operator-supplied values.

input.description: Hidden-input prompt for operator-supplied secrets set with `mm secret set` or `mm secret rotate`.

allow-shared-volumes.description:
Lets a service with role `database` or `queue` mount a shared
volume, which mm otherwise refuses: a shared volume is a network
mount, slower than local disk and without the locking guarantees
such a service needs.

autoscale.description:
On a cluster target: follow the load between `scale.min` and
`scale.max`, the one required key (`domain::autoscale`).

config-files.description: Files the service ships with, by their path in the container.

development.description:
`on`, `optional` or `off` in the development environment; without
it, the module's.

drain.description:
On a cluster target: how long a container of this service that
leaves (a rolling update replaces it, it moves, or it is scaled
away) keeps serving what is in flight once no node sends it new
requests, such as `30s`. Then it gets its stop signal and its
`stop_grace_period`. The default is `1m`.

environments.description: Environments in which this service runs; an empty list enables all.

hardening.description:
The defaults of `hardening: strict` this service leaves out, each
with a reason: `hardening: {except: {read-only: "writes its cache"}}`.

health.description:
On a cluster target: what the service's node does with a container
that keeps failing its health check. Without it, the node restarts
one that stays unhealthy for 3m, at most 5 times in 1h.

host-network.description:
Lets the service run in its host's network namespace
(`network_mode: host` in its Compose file) on this machine. The
value says why, and the plan shows it. On a remote host the host's
policy decides instead.

host-user-namespace.description:
On a remote host that runs Podman, keeps this service in the host's
user namespace instead of one of its own (`userns: auto`). The value
says why; a service that mounts a shared volume needs it.

http-port.description: A persisted HTTP selection made explicitly or by the guided editor.

placement.description:
Which nodes of a cluster target run this service, one container on
each: a node name, a group name, `all` for every node, or a list of
those. Without it the service runs on the target's first node. The
names must exist on the environment's target.

replicas.description:
On a cluster target: the containers the service runs over its nodes
when nothing scales it; default one per node, and `autoscale`'s `min`.

update.description:
How a deployment replaces this service's containers. Every key has
a default: stop the old container first, one node at a time, and
roll the deployment back when the new one fails.

ServiceConfigFileConfig.description:
A file the service ships with, mounted read-only at the path that is
its key under `config-files`. Exactly one of `file` and `template`
says where it comes from.

environments.description:
Environments in which the file is mounted; an empty list means all
of the service's.

file.description: A file of the module, shipped as it is.

template.description:
A file of the module in which every `{{ KEY }}` is replaced by the
environment's binding of that key.

uid.description:
The numeric user that owns the file. Without it the file belongs
to the user mm runs as on the host.

except.description:
The defaults of `hardening: strict` this service does not take, each
with the reason, which the plan shows.

environments.description:
Environments in which the file is mounted and its secret required;
an empty list means all of the service's.

ServiceSelection.description: Services an add-on applies to: all of them, none, or a named list.

after.description:
Stacks a deployment rolls out before this one. Without it, stacks
roll out in name order.

shared-volumes.description:
Top-level Compose volumes of this stack that are one directory on
every node of a cluster target: the target's storage node keeps the
files and the other nodes mount them over the mesh. For files that
replicas share, such as uploads. Not for databases: a shared volume
is slower than local disk and does not give the locking guarantees a
database needs. On a target that names one host they are ordinary
volumes.

StoreNodes.description:
The Raft members of a managed store: every node of the target, or the
nodes named. Three or five.

TargetProviderConfig.description: What a target changes about one of the project's `providers:`.

address.description:
Where this target's hosts reach the store, for example
`https://127.0.0.1:8200` when it runs on the host itself, or a mesh
address. Replaces the provider's own `address` on this target.

UpRuleConfig.description:
`autoscale.metric.up`: add a container when the average is above
`greater` for `for`.

parallelism.description:
How many nodes of a cluster target replace the service's stack at
the same time. The default is 1.

UpdateFailure.description: What a deployment does when this service does not become healthy.

oneOf.description: Every node the deployment changed returns to what it ran before.

The deployment stops where it is and changes nothing more, so the
failed container can be looked at. `mm deploy rollback` returns the
nodes to what they ran before.

UpdateOrder.description:
Whether a service's new container starts before or after the old one
stops.

oneOf.description: The engine stops the old container, then starts the new one.

The new container starts next to the old one, and the old one stops
once the new one is healthy and the other nodes resolve it. Not for
a service that publishes a host port or sets `container_name`.

access.description: Level per environment name, or `*` for every remote environment.

machine.description: A CI or automation identity rather than a person.

agent.description:
The key of this user's AI agent (`mm key create --agent`). It gets
the user's access limited by the `agents:` block, never more.

expires.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`; the key stops working at the start of that UTC day.
